The whole set of rules, parts and files that make a product look and behave consistently
A named design value (color, size, duration) stored once and reused everywhere
Raw value tier (blue.500 = a color) with no meaning attached
Meaning tier that points at a primitive (color.bg.accent -> blue.500)
Tier scoped to one component (button.primary.bg)
A token whose value is a reference to another token
One set of values for the same tokens, e.g. light or dark, compact or comfortable
A named combination of modes and brand values applied to the whole system
W3C Design Tokens Community Group format, stable version 2025.10
DTCG module that says which token files and modes combine into a theme
Ordered shades of one hue from light to dark
Grays (pure or tinted) used for text, backgrounds and borders
The one color used for primary actions, selection and focus
Success, warning, error and info colors
How different two colors are in lightness; WCAG 2.2 needs 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text and UI parts
Web Content Accessibility Guidelines; version 2.2, level AA is the usual target
Perceptual color space (lightness, chroma, hue) used to build even ramps
A separate mapping of colors for dark backgrounds, not an inversion
A background layer that content sits on; systems stack several surface levels
A font family, such as Inter or SF Pro
The fixed list of text sizes the product uses, often base x ratio^n
Vertical space each line of text takes
Space added or removed between letters (tracking)
How thick the letters are, from thin (100) to black (900)
The fixed list of gaps and paddings, usually multiples of 4px
Space inside an element, between its edge and its content
Space outside an element, between it and its neighbours
Space between items laid out in a row, column or grid
Columns and gutters that line up content across a page
Screen width at which the layout changes
How tightly packed the interface is (compact vs comfortable)
The tappable area of a control; WCAG 2.2 AA minimum 24 by 24 CSS px, platforms ask 44pt (Apple) or 48dp (Android)
How rounded corners are
How far a surface seems to float above the one below it
Drawn darkness under an element that shows elevation
How long an animation lasts, typically 100-300 ms for UI
How an animation speeds up and slows down over its duration
Physics-based motion defined by stiffness and damping instead of a fixed duration
A user setting (prefers-reduced-motion) asking for less animation
The visible outline showing which control the keyboard is on
A small symbol that stands for an action or object
A reusable interface part such as a button or text field
A styled version of a component, e.g. primary or secondary button
How a component looks in a situation: hover, pressed, focused, disabled, loading, error
The named parts a component is made of
A proven arrangement of components that solves a common task, such as a form or search
A page layout built from patterns, such as a dashboard or settings page
A readable file at the project root that records the design system's decisions for people and AI models
The one place a value is edited; everything else is generated from it
Turning design decisions into working code (tokens, CSS, components)
Figma's built-in named values with modes, the Figma equivalent of tokens
Model Context Protocol, the standard that lets an AI model use outside tools such as Figma or Paper
A folder of instructions and files an AI model loads to do a specific job well
A question where OpenDesigner asks whether you have something only a designer or a tool can make (logo, icons, photos)
Reading an example website, screenshot or file to learn its structure and quality, never its brand identity
A building block OpenDesigner can compute from a few inputs
A building block that can be read from a reference
A building block that needs a human creator, such as a logo
A building block an engineer can make with a named tool
A decision only the team can make, such as scope or audience
How detailed a part of the system is so far: sketch, defined or detailed
The first, low-detail pass over the whole system: a complete but coarse result
An automatic check that flags a design or code problem, such as too many font sizes
The order in which the eye notices things, set by size, weight, color and position
People see things that are close together or enclosed as one group
Bigger and closer targets are faster to hit
More choices take longer to decide between, unless they are grouped or searchable
Showing only what is needed now and revealing detail on request
The way an operating system expects controls and navigation to behave
Following the platform's own controls and styling instead of a custom brand style
